A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching material moved between sections.

before.justification: V1 reports original token-alignment measurements, spectral analyses, sparse-retrieval evaluations, and interpretability case studies.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds a linguistic analysis of words corresponding to aligned tokens.

M1.justification: Process 1, decoder projection, first-principal-component adjustment, document sparsification, and query expansion remain unchanged. The new linguistic probe analyzes the existing method rather than modifying it.

E1.justification: Appendix C adds MS MARCO query texts alongside documents in the alignment study, whereas v1's MS MARCO alignment checks used documents. The existing Wiki1M/SNLI coverage and four retrieval benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: V2 Section 6 newly reports preliminary nonalignment checks involving GTE, Contriever, and E5, beyond v1's SBERT/SimCSE examples, and the limitations identify DPR as an exception. These are qualitative small-model comparisons; Table 3's retrieval comparator set is unchanged.

E3.justification: The new linguistic probe uses 500 MS MARCO query–document pairs, LLM2Vec's top-five aligned tokens, and comparisons with linguistic annotations. Existing alignment samples, retrieval metrics, model configurations, and K/M hyperparameter grids are unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix C and Figure 5 examine whether aligned tokens originate from particular parts of speech, named entities, or dependency categories. Existing spectral analyses, principal-component interventions, instruction/training-data cases, and retrieval sensitivity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added linguistic frequency plots do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: V2 adds linguistic frequency results, reporting concentration in nouns, adjectives, and proper nouns, and an analytically estimated 13.4% FLOP ratio. Original plots and retrieval scores remain unchanged; for example, sparse LLM2Vec still scores 0.404/0.326/0.669/0.481 in Table 3.

T1.justification: Appendix E.4 adds a computational-cost derivation comparing N(2d−1) dense operations with N(M̂+K) sparse operations and their ratio in Equation 19. Existing spectral derivations and alignment-metric definitions are retained, with renumbering and notation cleanup.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims about key-token alignment, first-principal-component changes, and sparse retrieval preserving approximately 80% of dense performance. The additional analyses do not redefine the principal contributions.

C2.justification: The limitations now acknowledge DPR as an exception to the earlier negative statement about traditional PLMs. V2 also qualifies the FLOP estimate as implementation-dependent. V1's explanation connecting sentence/document length to LAR/GAR differences is omitted, although the corresponding results remain.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly documents spaCy segmentation and linguistic annotation, followed by word-level tokenization and matching against aligned tokens. Existing checkpoint access information, retrieval instructions, software versions, and A100/CUDA specifications are retained.

R1.justification: New Section 6 substantially expands research positioning: it distinguishes the work from embedding-inversion methods and explicitly acknowledges Ram et al. (2023)'s closely related token-alignment finding. It explains differences in model coverage, spectral explanation, and applications, rather than merely adding citations.

P1.justification: V2 renames Section 3.4, moves the quantitative analysis into Appendix B, reorganizes the appendices, and inserts Related Work before the conclusion. Local prose and notation edits accompany these changes; most existing exposition remains intact.

P2.justification: V1 Figures 2 and 7 are consolidated into v2 Figure 4, and a new three-panel linguistic Figure 5 is added. Table 3 moves and changes '+ Spar.' to 'to Spar.' Original graphical content is otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: V2 improves attribution and contextualization by acknowledging the closely related Ram et al. work and qualifying the PLM limitation. Its linguistic probe adds useful evidence about aligned tokens. These are targeted gains: the central methods and benchmark evidence remain unchanged, while the new 13.4% FLOP estimate is an approximate scoring calculation rather than measured end-to-end efficiency.
